activities.name: Similan and Surin Islands
activities.note: Mu Ko Similan National Park; day trips and liveaboards run from Phuket and Khao Lak

windows.reason: the national park shuts for about five months each year so the reefs can recover, and because the southwest monsoon makes the crossing unsafe. Recent closures have run mid-May to mid-October
the closure starts and ends mid-month, so roughly half of each is shut - confirm the year's exact dates before booking
the park is open and the Andaman Sea is at its calmest and clearest

activities.name: Adang and Rawi islands (Tarutao)
activities.note: the Tarutao National Park islands reached by boat from Ko Lipe; Lipe and Tarutao themselves stay open all year

windows.reason: the park closes the Adang-Rawi archipelago from 16 May to 14 October because of strong winds and high waves
the seasonal closure begins on 16 May and lifts after 14 October, so half the month is shut

activities.name: Ang Thong Marine National Park
activities.note: the marine park in the Gulf of Thailand off Koh Samui, visited on day trips

windows.reason: the park's annual rest period runs from 1 November to 15 December
still shut for the annual rest period until 15 December; trips resume in the second half of the month

activities.name: Diving off Koh Tao
activities.note: the Gulf of Thailand runs on a different calendar from the Andaman coast, and Koh Tao can be dived all year

windows.reason: the Gulf's short monsoon brings heavy rain, wind and reduced visibility at the dive sites
calm seas and good visibility after the monsoon has passed

activities.name: Phu Kradueng summit hike
activities.note: a mountain national park in Loei, booked through the park's queue app

windows.reason: the park closes for four months every rainy season to let the forest recover and reduce accidents; reopens 1 October
the cool season, when visitor numbers peak; days average around 15°C and nights can drop to zero

activities.name: Songkran water festival
activities.note: Thai New Year, a national holiday

windows.reason: the three-day Thai New Year holiday on 13–15 April, when streets close for water fights

activities.name: Yi Peng and Loy Krathong in Chiang Mai
activities.note: sky lanterns may not be released in the city itself; the mass releases are ticketed events outside it

windows.reason: held over the full moon of the second Lanna lunar month, usually in November; the exact nights shift each year

activities.name: Phuket Vegetarian Festival
activities.note: processions, firecrackers and meat-free food centred on the Chinese shrines of Phuket Town

windows.reason: nine days at the start of the ninth Chinese lunar month, usually late September or early October

activities.name: Phi Ta Khon ghost festival
activities.note: a masked three-day festival in Dan Sai, Loei

windows.reason: three days usually in late June or early July; the dates follow the lunar calendar and are chosen by local mediums each year
